name: CHI
fullName: ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
notes: Main papers track. No separate abstract deadline. Submission includes videos and supplementary materials. The official 24-hour contingency grace period is not included in the deadline shown. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

paperFit.emphasis: User needs, task outcomes and experience

guide.contribution: New interaction techniques, tools or design findings tied to a concrete human activity. Recent work connects interface decisions to communication, creative practice or input performance, explaining how the design changes what people can do and how they experience it.
guide.evidence: Evaluation often combines formative research with controlled tasks or deployment in everyday settings. Papers examine task performance, participation, workload or creative outcomes alongside observations and interviews, using the population and usage context that motivated the design.

comparisons.difference: CHI connects an interface to user needs and activities, using interviews, task studies or deployment. IEEE VR more directly tests immersive effects such as embodiment, presence, comfort and performance inside a virtual environment.

CHI studies interfaces across activities such as communication, input and creative work. HRI focuses on people working with robots, testing how autonomy, physical assistance and robot communication affect performance and trust.

name: IEEE VR
fullName: IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces
notes: One unified submission and review process for IEEE TVCG and conference-only papers. A paper abstract is required seven days before the paper. Notification times are not specified.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG)
publication.note: Unified review assigns accepted papers to the journal or conference proceedings.

guide.contribution: Interaction methods and immersive systems that change embodiment, communication or movement in virtual environments. Recent papers connect technical changes in visual, audio or tactile feedback to measurable differences in what users perceive and accomplish, including accessibility applications.
guide.evidence: Controlled comparisons measure task performance together with presence, embodiment, workload or discomfort. Social interaction papers also examine communication and social presence. Studies isolate the feedback or representation being changed and report which outcomes improve and which remain unchanged.

comparisons.difference: IEEE VR tests how visual, audio or tactile feedback affects immersive tasks, presence and comfort. ACM SAP isolates perceptual effects, measuring judgments, detection thresholds or eye movements as the stimulus changes.

Recent IEEE VR work tests embodiment, immersive communication and accessibility. Recent ISMAR work also develops scene capture and sensing methods, measuring reconstruction quality, prediction accuracy and task completion.

name: ISMAR
fullName: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality
notes: Unified IEEE TVCG journal and conference paper track. The 2027 site confirms Kobe, Japan, but the conference dates and paper deadlines are still TBA; estimates use the verified 2026 schedule.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG)
publication.note: Unified review assigns accepted papers to the journal or conference proceedings.

paperFit.emphasis: Accuracy and performance in XR tasks

guide.contribution: Methods for spatial interaction, scene acquisition and sensing in AR, MR or VR. Recent work integrates graphics or machine learning with an interaction problem, showing how representations, environmental information or sensor signals improve a specific XR task.
guide.evidence: Papers compare task accuracy and completion time, reconstruction results or sensor-based prediction against relevant alternatives. Evaluations vary input conditions, environments or movement, while interaction studies also collect preference and perceived success to explain performance differences.

comparisons.difference: ISMAR includes spatial interfaces and scene capture, measured through task performance and reconstruction quality. IEEE AIxVR focuses on AI in XR, testing prediction robustness or whether an adaptive system improves training and workload.

Recent ISMAR work tests scene acquisition, mobile sensing and spatial interaction. Recent IEEE VR work tests immersive feedback and representation, measuring embodiment, presence, communication and comfort.

name: VRST
fullName: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
notes: Main papers track. The abstract is required one week before the full paper. Includes the officially extended revision and final-notification dates. No official 2027 schedule was found. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Practical VR hardware, interaction techniques and computational components that improve a defined task. Recent papers range from combined desktop and spatial input devices to efficient gesture recognition and grasping methods, making the connection between implementation choices and interaction performance explicit.
guide.evidence: Interaction studies compare completion time, accuracy, workload and user experience across techniques. Computational papers use datasets, model comparisons and ablations, reporting recognition quality alongside parameter count or computation. Evaluation measures the claimed improvement at the relevant system or interaction level.

comparisons.difference: Recent VRST work evaluates input devices, gesture recognition and grasping methods through accuracy, completion time and computation. Recent IEEE VR work also evaluates the immersive experience, including embodiment, presence and discomfort.

VRST often evaluates a VR device or component through recognition accuracy, task performance and runtime. CHI also investigates the activity around the interface, using user research and deployment to explain needs and outcomes.

name: ACM SAP
notes: Abstract submission is required. The paper deadline was extended from April 28. This schedule covers SAP proceedings papers; invited TAP journal papers have a separate second review and final deadline. Notification release has no exact time.

publication.note: Selected papers undergo a second review cycle and publish in TAP instead of the proceedings.

paperFit.scope: Perception of graphics and virtual humans

guide.contribution: Findings or models that explain how people perceive visual, motion or multisensory content. Recent papers isolate expression intensity, rendering conditions or conflicting sensory cues, connecting perceptual differences to choices in avatar presentation and interaction design.
guide.evidence: Controlled stimulus manipulations are paired with judgments, eye tracking, detection thresholds or model fits. Analyses distinguish perceptual dimensions and individual differences, showing which stimulus changes affect perception and where a proposed explanation fits observed behavior.

comparisons.difference: ACM SAP isolates how a stimulus changes perception, using controlled judgments, eye tracking or detection thresholds. IEEE VR tests how such changes affect an immersive task, including performance, presence and comfort.

ACM SAP studies how people perceive expressions, motion and sensory cues. ACM IVA develops the agent behavior behind an interaction, testing dialogue consistency, believability and negotiation or training outcomes.

name: IEEE AIxVR
fullName: IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and eXtended and Virtual Reality
notes: Formerly IEEE AIVR; renamed AIxVR in 2024. This schedule covers full/short papers, extended from September 17 to September 21, 2026. Notifications are only specified as early-to-mid-November 2026, so no exact notification date is shown. Separate 2027 work-in-progress and demo/video tracks close October 29, 2026; workshops set their own deadlines. The source states AoE but gives no exact clock time.

core.note: No matching entry found by acronym and full title; this is not an Unranked classification.

publication.note: Selected papers are invited to submit extended versions; the 2027 call does not name the journal.

guide.contribution: AI methods or adaptive systems that address a concrete XR limitation, such as motion prediction or personalized training. Recent papers connect the learning approach to deployment conditions, including calibration errors, real-time workload estimates and changes to the user's task.
guide.evidence: Model evaluations use public and captured data, reference methods and realistic perturbations. Adaptive applications compare against a fixed or conventional system using objective task performance, subjective workload and interviews, reporting whether adaptation changes outcomes as well as user preference.

comparisons.difference: IEEE AIxVR tests AI-based prediction and adaptation in XR, including robustness to calibration errors and effects on training. ISMAR also includes scene capture and spatial interfaces evaluated through reconstruction quality and task performance.

IEEE AIxVR applies learning to XR sensing and adaptation, measuring prediction accuracy, workload or training performance. ACM IVA focuses on social agents, measuring consistency across conversations, believability and interaction outcomes.

name: ACM IVA
fullName: ACM International Conference on Intelligent Virtual Agents
notes: Full papers track with a separate abstract deadline. Submission dates include the published extensions; these extensions may not recur. The IVA series announces Reykjavik in September 2027, but exact event dates and paper deadlines are not published; estimates use the 2026 schedule. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Agent architectures and behavior models that produce coherent, adaptive social interaction. Recent papers combine language models with explicit beliefs or intentions, maintain consistent agent values, or adapt negotiation behavior to human emotion and preferences in a concrete interaction scenario.
guide.evidence: Studies compare agent architectures or behavior policies through conversations, training scenarios or negotiation. Evaluations combine consistency and task outcomes with believability, perceived alignment and satisfaction; extended dialogues test whether behavior remains coherent beyond an isolated response.

comparisons.difference: ACM IVA develops agent reasoning and responses, evaluating dialogue consistency, negotiation and believability. ACM SAP studies perception of the resulting presentation, using controlled changes to expressions, motion or sensory cues.

ACM IVA studies conversational architectures and adaptive social behavior. HRI also studies physical robot assistance and shared autonomy, where task completion, cognitive load and trust in the robot become central outcomes.

name: HRI
fullName: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
topics: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
notes: Full papers track. Short contributions and alt.HRI have separate deadlines. Late-breaking reports close December 8, 2026; videos and demos close November 20. These are distinct from the main full-paper track shown here.

publication.note: Nominated papers needing further work may transfer for continued journal review. This is not automatic journal publication.

guide.contribution: Robot interfaces, collaborative behaviors or design findings that address how people understand and work with robots. Recent papers connect autonomy and hardware capabilities to human control, assistance needs or communication in the physical environment, including accessible assistive systems.
guide.evidence: Evidence ranges from interviews with intended users to controlled robot tasks and integrated system case studies. Papers examine performance, cognitive load, trust or practical communication capability, selecting measures that expose the interaction consequences of the robot's design and behavior.

comparisons.difference: HRI tests how robot autonomy and physical assistance affect people, measuring task performance, workload and trust. CHI covers a wider range of interfaces and activities, often combining user research with task studies or deployment.

Recent HRI work studies assistive manipulation and robot communication in physical settings. ACM IVA focuses on how agents reason and converse, testing behavioral consistency, believability and negotiation outcomes.
